classifications.rationale: The covered agencies are mandatorily directed to publish proposed Common Rule revisions; the segment initiates and organizes rulemaking, while any binding legal consequence would arise only from later final rules.
classifications.evidence: shall promptly jointly publish in the Federal Register the following proposed revisions to the Common Rule as it affects classified research

classifications.rationale: HHS is assigned coordination responsibility and the agencies must issue specified proposals and solicit comment, but the segment does not itself enact the proposals or require their final adoption.
classifications.evidence: The agencies shall jointly propose to prohibit waiver of informed consent for classified research.

classifications.rationale: The OSTP Director must review an appeal but retains authority to choose whether the project is approved or disapproved, so no particular later legal outcome is dictated.
classifications.evidence: The Director of OSTP shall review the IRB's decision and approve or disapprove the project

classifications.rationale: The segment inseparably combines administrative determinations, reporting, and rulemaking duties with a presently operative prohibition on conducting covered research without personal agency-head approval.
classifications.evidence: Agencies may not conduct any classified human research project subject to the Common Rule unless the agency head has personally approved the specific project.

classifications.rationale: The OSTP Director is assigned mandatory reporting and publication tasks, and the accompanying definitions clarify the memorandum's administration without independently changing substantive rights or status.
classifications.evidence: The Director of OSTP shall report the total number of classified research projects and participating subjects to the President

classifications.rationale: The memorandum itself prospectively imposes, beginning one year later, a substantive condition barring agencies from conducting or supporting classified human research unless they have promulgated the required rule.
classifications.evidence: no agency shall conduct or support classified human research without having proposed and promulgated the Common Rule
